title: Crude oil & cracking
examples: How does a refinery separate all the different parts of oil?
What is the difference between distillation and cracking?
Can we use the oil we get from crude oil for things other than fuel?

explain.say: Today we learn about crude oil and how we use it.
First we look at fractional distillation to separate the oil.
The process separates substances based on their boiling points.
Next we discuss cracking, which breaks large molecules into smaller ones.
These smaller useful molecules are what we use as fuels every day.
In everyday life, think about a car filling up at a petrol station.

faq.q: How is fractional distillation different from simple distillation?
faq.a: Simple distillation separates liquids with very different boiling points. Fractional distillation uses a fractionating column to separate liquids with boiling points that are close together.
asks: What is the difference between the two types of distillation?
Do I need a fractionating column for all liquids?

faq.q: What is the main purpose of cracking crude oil?
faq.a: The main purpose of cracking is to break down very large, less useful hydrocarbon molecules into smaller, more valuable ones like gasoline.
asks: Why do we need to crack the oil?
Does cracking make the oil better?

faq.q: Are all fuels derived from crude oil?
faq.a: While most common fuels like petrol and diesel come from crude oil, some fuels, like electricity, come from different sources.
asks: Can we get fuel from somewhere else?
Is oil the only source of energy?

faq.a: A hydrocarbon is a compound made up only of hydrogen and carbon atoms. These form the basis of most fossil fuels.

faq.q: What happens to the oil residue left after distillation?
faq.a: The heavy residue, called bitumen, is left at the bottom. It is used for roofing and making roads, not usually as fuel.
asks: Is the bottom part of the oil useful?

facts: Crude oil is a mixture of many different hydrocarbons.
Fractional distillation separates components by boiling point differences.
Cracking breaks large, complex hydrocarbons into smaller, useful ones.
Gasoline has a lower boiling point than diesel.

quiz.say: Which process separates oil components based on boiling points?
quiz.why: This process uses temperature differences to collect different fractions.

wrong.1: Cracking breaks molecules, it does not separate them by boiling point.
wrong.2: Combustion is burning, which releases energy, it is not a separation technique.
wrong.3: Condensation is cooling vapour back to liquid, it is a step, not the whole process.

quiz.say: If a fuel has a very high boiling point, where will it collect in the column?
quiz.why: Substances with high boiling points condense lower down in the column.

wrong.1: The top is where the coolest temperatures are, so only very light gases collect there.
wrong.2: The condenser cools the vapour, but the fraction collects at a specific level.
wrong.3: The residue does collect at the bottom, which is the lowest point.

quiz.say: What is the main product obtained from cracking that powers cars?
quiz.why: Cracking is used to create smaller, useful molecules, and gasoline is a key product.

wrong.1: Bitumen is a heavy residue used for roads, not a primary car fuel.
wrong.2: Crude oil is the raw mixture before any separation or breaking down happens.
wrong.3: Diesel is also a fuel, but gasoline is the specific product often targeted for car use from cracking.
